title: Island Count
statement:
Count the islands on a map made of land and water cells.

Contract
- `grid` is a rectangular `char[][]` (possibly empty) containing only `'1'` (land) and `'0'` (water).
- An island is a maximal group of land cells connected through shared edges: up, down, left, or right. Diagonal neighbors are not connected.
- Return the number of islands.
- Your method may modify the grid, for example to mark visited cells; tests do not rely on it being unchanged.

Examples
- Rows `110`, `010`, `001` contain 2 islands.
- A grid of only water contains 0 islands.
- Rows `101`, `010`, `101` contain 5 islands, because diagonal cells do not connect.
hints: Every island is a connected component of land cells, so count how many separate components exist.
Scan the grid; when you reach a land cell you have not visited, count one island and explore everything connected to it so it is never counted again.

Explore with an explicit stack or queue, marking cells visited as you add them (a visited array, or overwrite the cell). Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space, where n is the number of grid cells.
inputSyntax: Input: grid rows of 0 and 1 characters separated by spaces, for example: 1101 0100 0011
